title: What if every paper were AI-written?
blurb: To separate what a lab writes about from how it words it, we rewrote the abstract of every paper in the study with the same language model and the same instruction, so that all wording is AI wording and equal across papers. We then measured diversity and novelty on those rewrites exactly as on the originals, using the same embedding models, the same topic clusters and the same size-matched draws. Where the two corpora move together, the change is in the content; where they differ, the difference is due to wording.
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, revision a09a35458c702b33eeacc393d103063234e8bc28, vLLM 0.8.3, bf16, greedy decoding (temperature 0, seed 20261104)
prompt: Here is the abstract of a research paper titled "{title}". Rewrite it as a polished academic abstract: improve its clarity, flow and academic style. Keep every claim, number, method name and technical term exactly as given; do not add or drop any information. Keep roughly the same length (about {n} words). Return only the rewritten abstract, as plain text in a single paragraph.
second_style: paraphrase (rewrite in the model's own words), 4,996 papers stratified by school and year, as a robustness check
filter: a rewrite is dropped when it was cut off, refused, much shorter than its source, loses 25% or more of the source's numbers, adds many new numbers, or loses 25% or more of the source's named methods (acronyms, CamelCase, names with digits); the comparison always uses the same papers in both corpora
limits: only abstracts are rewritten (titles stay as written; full texts are too large)
one rewriting model and one prompt; the paraphrase style is the robustness check
a rewrite can still drift in small details (a hand read of 20 found 4 minor ones)
pairwise cosine distance on centred vectors is close to 1 for every set and carries little signal; Vendi, dispersion and topic entropy are the informative measures
